messages:
margo: heads-up: customer saw a sudden token spike during a mid-request model swap. looks like router routed the same request to two model variants and both provisonals confirmed. repro attached.
aj: ouch. can you paste the minimal logs?
margo: logs:
```
2026-07-02T17:02:10.000Z [router] session=s-9 req=req-42 route=hosted-v2 event=provisional tx=tx-a model=v2
2026-07-02T17:02:10.050Z [router] session=s-9 req=req-42 route=hosted-v1 event=provisional tx=tx-b model=v1 reason=model_swap
2026-07-02T17:02:10.120Z [ledger] confirm tx=tx-a tokens=150
2026-07-02T17:02:17.200Z [ledger] confirm tx=tx-b tokens=150
```
margo: ledger counts both confirms -> +150 tokens twice.
chip: this is different from prefetch races. here the router intentionally forked the request during a swap; both workers treated their provisional as canonical.
yelena: two possible patterns for fix:
- router should cancel earlier provisional when it triggers a duplicate route for same req_id (emit cancel event to ledger)
- ledger should dedupe confirms by request_id + prefix range, preferring the earliest confirmed or router-declared canonical route
aj: router cancel helps but network losses could mean cancel never arrives. ledger-side dedupe by request_id seems safer.
chip: ledger dedupe rule: if confirms share the same request_id, collapse to single confirm and emit reconciliation audit. we already have request ids in events so not too invasive.
yelena: console UX: surface model variant per provisional and mark "swapped" events. ops need to see when model swap caused duplicate claims.
ops-bot: billing-alert session=s-9 delta=+150 created by billing-bot
margo: mitigation plan: 1) short-term: router emits a cancel on previous provisional when issuing new route for same req_id (best-effort) 2) medium-term: add ledger rule to dedupe confirms by request_id and emit reconciled_confirm audit events 3) console: add request-level model timeline showing provisional/confirm/cancel (yelena)
aj: telemetry: add metric model_swap_dupes.count and an alert if >5 in 5m across a single region.
chip: implementation note: dedupe must be idempotent and deterministic. choose canonical confirm = first confirm that includes an explicit router-canonical flag, else earliest confirm wins.
yelena: also update rollout docs: when we do mid-request model swaps (canary traffic steering) we should include invariant that router will cancel prior provisonals for the same request_id.
margo: I'll draft RFC with repro, router-cancel PR, ledger-dedupe design, and console mockups. aiming for canary in staging next week.
aj: assign owners: router-cancel (margo), ledger-dedupe (chip), console timeline (yelena). billing-bot: created ticket BILL-999 for reconciliation audit events.
margo: thanks all. ping me if you want to run the repro together. :thumbsup:
